$comment: Plain-language explanations for Node.js / TypeScript findings (bot/lib/adapters/node.ts). Keyed by finding kind. See common.json for the format.

codemod.express5.plainTitle: Update the code for Express 5 (official codemod)
codemod.express5.inPlainWords: Express 5 removed some old shortcuts. The official Express codemod rewrites them for you.
codemod.express5.whatWeFound: The app uses Express {fromExpress}. The codemod {name} will update {count} file(s).
codemod.express5.whyItMatters: Express 5 removed calls like req.param(), res.send(404) and redirect('back'). Code that still uses them breaks: some calls throw, others quietly send the wrong response.
codemod.express5.whatWillHappen: The codemod rewrites each removed call to its Express 5 replacement. Every change is committed so you can review it.
codemod.express5.ifApproved: The code matches Express 5 and the tests run against it.
codemod.express5.ifLocked: Locked files keep the Express 4 calls while the app runs on Express 5. Requests that hit them fail or return the wrong status, so tests that cover those routes fail at the Test step.
manualSteps: Rewrite each removed call listed below by hand (see the Express 5 migration guide).
Run the tests that hit those routes.

express-api.codemod.inPlainWords: This line uses {api}, which Express 5 removed. The codemod changes it to {replacement}.
express-api.codemod.whyItMatters: On Express 5 this call no longer does what it did: it either throws (req.param) or sends the wrong thing (res.send(404) sends "404" as the body with status 200).
express-api.codemod.whatWillHappen: The Express codemod rewrites it to {replacement}.
express-api.codemod.ifApproved: The line is rewritten and behaves the same on Express 5.
express-api.codemod.ifLocked: Locking keeps the whole file ({file}) unchanged, so every Express 4 call in it stays. On Express 5 the route breaks: the TypeScript build or the tests that call it fail at the Test step.
manualSteps: Replace {api} with {replacement}.
Run the test for this route.

rules.package-json.inPlainWords: The versions of Node, TypeScript, Express and their type packages are raised to the target.
rules.package-json.whyItMatters: This is the upgrade itself. Without it, the project keeps installing the old versions.
rules.package-json.whatWillHappen: The rules set each version range to the target (Node {targetNode}, TypeScript {targetTs}) and npm install fetches them.
rules.package-json.ifApproved: npm install brings in the new versions and the tests run against them.
rules.package-json.ifLocked: package.json keeps the old versions, so nothing is really upgraded. Locking it also undoes the codemod's package.json edits. The checks step reports that the targets weren't reached and the run fails.
manualSteps: Update the version ranges shown below by hand.
Run npm install and npm test.

rules.tsconfig.inPlainWords: TypeScript {targetTs} rejects some old compiler options, so they're replaced with the current ones.
rules.tsconfig.whatWeFound: {fileName} uses options TypeScript {targetTs} deprecated or changed: {details}.
rules.tsconfig.whyItMatters: TypeScript 6 turns these deprecated options into errors and no longer loads @types packages automatically, so the build stops before any test runs.
rules.tsconfig.whatWillHappen: The rules replace or remove each option and add the types the project needs.
rules.tsconfig.ifLocked: tsconfig.json keeps the old options. TypeScript {targetTs} stops with errors (for example, moduleResolution "node" is deprecated), so npm test fails at the Test step.
manualSteps: Apply the option changes shown below.
Run npx tsc --noEmit.

rules.nvmrc.plainTitle: Set the Node version file to {targetNode}
rules.nvmrc.inPlainWords: The file that tells nvm and other tools which Node to use is updated.
rules.nvmrc.whyItMatters: Developers and some CI setups use this file to pick the Node version.
rules.nvmrc.whatWillHappen: The version in {fileName} is set to {targetNode}.
rules.nvmrc.ifApproved: Everyone using nvm switches to Node {targetNode}.
rules.nvmrc.ifLocked: The dry run isn't affected, but developers keep running the old Node locally and may see different results.
manualSteps: Put {targetNode} in {fileName}.

rules.other.inPlainWords: Small configuration edits from the Node rules.
rules.other.whyItMatters: They keep the configuration in line with the target versions.
rules.other.whatWillHappen: The rules apply the edits listed.
rules.other.ifLocked: The file keeps its old content; the edits become manual work.
manualSteps: Apply the edits shown below.

install.inPlainWords: npm downloads the upgraded packages so the tests run against them.
install.whyItMatters: Without installing, the tests would still run the old packages and prove nothing.
install.whatWillHappen: npm install runs after the rule edits. The lockfile is refreshed if there is one.
install.ifApproved: Dependencies are installed with the new versions.
install.ifLocked: This is project-wide and can't be locked. Marking it manual only adds a note to the report; the install still runs because the tests need it.
manualSteps: Review the lockfile diff for unexpected major version jumps.

node-api.removed.inPlainWords: This line calls a Node API that was removed, so it throws on Node {node}.
node-api.removed.whyItMatters: Calling a removed API throws an error at runtime, so the feature using it breaks.
node-api.removed.whatWillHappen: No codemod rewrites it. If a test fails, the AI fix-up may replace it with {replacement}.
node-api.removed.ifApproved: Tests that reach this line fail; the AI fix-up gets a few tries.
node-api.removed.ifLocked: The AI fix-up can't touch the file, so the call stays and fails on Node {node}.
manualSteps: Replace {api} with {replacement}.
Run the code path that uses it.

node-api.deprecated.inPlainWords: This still works on Node {node} but is deprecated. Swap it for {replacement} when you can.
node-api.deprecated.whyItMatters: Deprecated APIs can print warnings, behave differently with unusual input, and may be removed in a later Node release.
node-api.deprecated.whatWillHappen: No codemod rewrites it. Nothing changes unless a test fails and the AI fix-up touches it.
node-api.deprecated.ifApproved: Keeps working on Node {node}; you may see a deprecation warning.
node-api.deprecated.ifLocked: Same as approving: it keeps working. The lock only stops the AI fix-up from editing this file.
manualSteps: Replace {api} with {replacement}.
Run the tests.

express-routing.plainTitle: Route path uses syntax Express 5 changed
express-routing.inPlainWords: Wildcards (*), optional parts (?) and regex groups in route paths are written differently in Express 5.
express-routing.whyItMatters: The codemod doesn't rewrite paths. On Express 5 this route either fails to register or stops matching the URLs it used to, so requests get 404s.
express-routing.ifApproved: Tests that hit this route likely fail; the AI fix-up may rewrite the path.
express-routing.ifLocked: The path stays in Express 4 syntax and the AI fix-up can't touch it, so the route breaks on Express 5.
manualSteps: Rewrite the path: name wildcards (/*splat) and use braces for optional parts ({/:id}).
Add or run a test that calls this route.

learnMore.label: Express: migrating to Express 5 (path route matching)

express-api.req-query.plainTitle: Code writes to req.query, which is read-only in Express 5
express-api.req-query.inPlainWords: Express 5 doesn't let you replace req.query any more.
express-api.req-query.whyItMatters: The assignment throws or is ignored, so code that relies on it reads the wrong values.
express-api.req-query.ifApproved: Tests covering it likely fail; the AI fix-up may move the value elsewhere.
express-api.req-query.ifLocked: The assignment stays and breaks on Express 5.
manualSteps: Store the parsed value in a new variable or res.locals instead.
Run the related tests.

native-addon.inPlainWords: {name} contains compiled code built for specific Node versions.
native-addon.whyItMatters: If there is no build for Node {node}, npm install fails or the app crashes when it loads the package.
native-addon.ifApproved: Nothing changes; if the version is too old, install or tests fail.
native-addon.ifLocked: package.json is locked, which also blocks the version bumps. Prefer 'Manual' unless you mean it.
manualSteps: Check {name}'s releases for Node {node} support.
Bump it by hand if needed and run npm install.

native-addon.node-sass.plainTitle: node-sass is dead; switch to sass
native-addon.node-sass.inPlainWords: node-sass has no builds for current Node, so install fails.
native-addon.node-sass.whyItMatters: npm install fails on Node {node}, and nothing after that can run.
native-addon.node-sass.ifApproved: npm install likely fails; the AI fix-up may swap the package.
native-addon.node-sass.ifLocked: package.json is locked, which also blocks the version bumps.
manualSteps: Replace node-sass with the sass package.
Run the style build.

dependency.request.inPlainWords: The request library has been deprecated since 2020.
dependency.request.whyItMatters: It gets no security fixes. It still works today.
dependency.request.ifLocked: package.json is locked, which also blocks the version bumps.
manualSteps: Move to the built-in fetch (Node 18+) or undici.

dependency.ts-node.plainTitle: ts-node may not work with TypeScript {typescript}
dependency.ts-node.inPlainWords: ts-node hasn't had a release for TypeScript 6; scripts that use it might break.
dependency.ts-node.whyItMatters: Dev scripts run through ts-node may fail after the upgrade, even if npm test passes.
dependency.ts-node.ifApproved: Check your scripts after the run.
dependency.ts-node.ifLocked: package.json is locked, which also blocks the version bumps.
manualSteps: Run your ts-node scripts after the upgrade.
Consider tsx or Node's built-in TypeScript support.

dependency.ts-jest.inPlainWords: This test tool version refuses the new TypeScript, so npm install stops.
dependency.ts-jest.whyItMatters: npm install fails with a peer-dependency error (ERESOLVE), so the tests can't run.
dependency.ts-jest.whatWillHappen: No automatic change; the AI fix-up may bump it.
dependency.ts-jest.ifApproved: Install likely fails first; the AI fix-up may upgrade ts-jest.
dependency.ts-jest.ifLocked: package.json is locked, which also blocks the version bumps.
manualSteps: Upgrade ts-jest and jest to versions that support TypeScript {typescript}.

dependency.manual.plainTitle: A dependency the rules won't change
dependency.manual.inPlainWords: The rules skipped this dependency on purpose; it needs a person to decide.
dependency.manual.whyItMatters: It may not work with the target versions.
dependency.manual.ifApproved: Nothing changes; check it after the run.
dependency.manual.ifLocked: The file is locked, which also blocks the other edits planned for it.
manualSteps: Make the change described here by hand.
Run npm install and npm test.

tsconfig.manual.plainTitle: A tsconfig change the rules can't make
tsconfig.manual.inPlainWords: This compiler option needs a person to decide.
tsconfig.manual.whyItMatters: TypeScript {targetTs} may refuse the old setting.
tsconfig.manual.whatWillHappen: Nothing is changed for this option.
tsconfig.manual.ifApproved: The build may fail; the AI fix-up may adjust it.
tsconfig.manual.ifLocked: tsconfig.json is locked, which also blocks the other tsconfig edits.
manualSteps: Make the change described here.
Run npx tsc --noEmit.

tsconfig.extends.inPlainWords: Some compiler settings come from another file the tool doesn't edit.
tsconfig.extends.whyItMatters: Deprecated options in the base file still break TypeScript {typescript}.
tsconfig.extends.ifApproved: The build may fail if the base file uses old options; the AI fix-up may override them.
tsconfig.extends.ifLocked: tsconfig.json is locked, which also blocks the planned tsconfig edits; the build likely fails.
manualSteps: Check {base} for moduleResolution, baseUrl and types.
Override them in tsconfig.json if needed.

tests.no-script.inPlainWords: There is no npm test, so the run can't prove the app still works.
tests.no-script.whyItMatters: The pipeline uses npm test to decide pass or fail.
tests.no-script.ifLocked: package.json is locked, which also blocks the version bumps.
manualSteps: Add a test script (node --test, vitest or jest).
Add at least one test.

package-manager.inPlainWords: This tool currently only upgrades npm projects.
package-manager.whyItMatters: Preflight refuses the run, and the lockfile wouldn't be updated.
package-manager.whatWillHappen: Nothing; the run stops at preflight.
manualSteps: Use npm for this migration, or upgrade with {manager} by hand.
